root_cause: CachingTest.LoadMultiWithConfig_race (caching_test.cpp, TEST_P around line 2644-2685) is a wall-clock-bounded stress/race test that repeatedly loads a MULTI-device model through ov::Core for ~2000ms, asserting mockPlugin->import_model(istream&, ...) is called a fixed number of times per iteration. Because the loop's stopping condition is time-based rather than iteration-count-based, and each iteration spins up concurrent import threads per device, a slow/loaded Windows CI runner can leave the final iteration's import_model call still in flight (one call 'unsatisfied and active') when TearDown() invokes Mock::VerifyAndClearExpectations immediately after the time budget expires. This is a known, previously-documented timing-sensitive test design (the file itself notes 'In case of sporadic failures - increase TEST_DURATION_MS 100x times for better reproducibility'), not a regression introduced by this commit. The triggering commit (#40094, GPU plugin sub-byte stride fix for RemoteTensorImpl) only touches src/plugins/intel_gpu/src/plugin/remote_tensor.cpp and its GPU functional test file; it does not touch caching_test.cpp, MULTI device logic, or any CPU inference-caching code, so it is unrelated to this failure.
reproduction_steps: Build ieFuncTests on Windows (Release) and run repeatedly under load: `ieFuncTests.exe --gtest_filter=CachingTest/CachingTest.LoadMultiWithConfig_race*`. Reproduction is intermittent and more likely on loaded/slower runners; running several times or under CPU contention increases odds of hitting the race window.
recommended_actions: Change the loop's stopping condition in LoadMulti_race/LoadMultiWithConfig_race (src/inference/tests/functional/caching_test.cpp, ~lines 2600-2685) to only check the time budget between fully-completed iterations, or add a short join/grace wait before the loop exits so in-flight async import_model calls finish before Mock verification runs in TearDown().
Mark this test as flaky-tolerant in CI (e.g., gtest retry/rerun-on-failure) given its documented non-determinism, rather than failing the whole post-commit pipeline on a sporadic miscount.
No action needed on the triggering PR #40094 (GPU sub-byte stride fix) - it does not touch caching_test.cpp or MULTI/inference caching code.
prevention_strategies: Avoid designing unit tests around hard wall-clock loop deadlines combined with asynchronous mock expectations; prefer deterministic iteration counts or explicit synchronization (e.g., wait for all pending import_model futures before the loop's time check) so TearDown() never races with in-flight async calls.
historical_context: This exact signature (pattern 9f9ea52f699d8da3) has now recurred four times: 2026-11-09, 2026-11-10, 2026-11-20, and this run (2026-11-21), always on Windows C++ unit tests jobs with the same import_model call-count mismatch in CachingTest.LoadMultiWithConfig_race/LoadMulti_race. The test's own source comment acknowledges sporadic failures are expected and suggests increasing TEST_DURATION_MS as a workaround, but no fix has been applied across any of the four occurrences.
